nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-01.title: Sum of cubes
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-01.body:
Use $x^3+y^3=(x+y)(x^2-xy+y^2)$ with $x=13$, $y=7$:
$$13^3+7^3=(13+7)(169-91+49)=20\cdot 127.$$
Since $20=2^2\cdot5$ and $127$ is prime (it is not divisible by $2,3,5,7,11$, and $11^2>127$), the factorization is $2^2\cdot5\cdot127$.

**Answer: $2^2\cdot 5\cdot 127$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-02.title: Edge cubes
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-02.body:
The big cube is $4\times4\times4$. A unit cube has exactly two painted faces when it lies on an edge of the big cube but is not a corner. Each of the $12$ edges has $4-2=2$ such cubes, so there are $12\cdot 2=24$.

**Answer: 24**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-02.title: Subtract the other types
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-02.body:
Of the $64$ cubes: $8$ corners (3 faces), $6\cdot 2^2=24$ face-centre cubes (1 face), and $2^3=8$ interior cubes (0 faces). The rest have exactly 2 faces: $64-8-24-8=24$.

**Answer: 24**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-03.title: Unwrap the floor
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-03.body:
The equation says $\left[\frac{3x}{2}\right]=6$, which holds exactly when $6\le \frac{3x}{2}<7$. Multiplying by $\frac23$: $4\le x<\frac{14}{3}$.

**Answer: $4\le x<\frac{14}{3}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-04.title: Two equations
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-04.body:
Put $x=3$ and $x=\frac13$:
$$2f(3)+f\!\left(\tfrac13\right)=\tfrac32,\qquad f(3)+2f\!\left(\tfrac13\right)=\tfrac16.$$
Double the first and subtract the second: $3f(3)=3-\frac16=\frac{17}{6}$, so $f(3)=\frac{17}{18}$.

**Answer: $\frac{17}{18}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-04.title: Find $f$ in general
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-04.body:
Replacing $x$ by $\frac1x$ gives $2f(\frac1x)+f(x)=\frac{1}{2x}$. Eliminating $f(\frac1x)$: $4f(x)-f(x)=x-\frac{1}{2x}$, so $f(x)=\frac{x}{3}-\frac{1}{6x}$. Then $f(3)=1-\frac1{18}=\frac{17}{18}$.

**Answer: $\frac{17}{18}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-05.title: Sine of a sum
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-05.body:
Let $A=\operatorname{Arcsin}\frac{12}{13}$ and $B=\operatorname{Arcsin}\frac{24}{25}$; both lie in $(0,\frac\pi2)$, so $\cos A=\frac5{13}$ and $\cos B=\frac7{25}$ (from the 5-12-13 and 7-24-25 right triangles). Then
$$x=\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B=\frac{12}{13}\cdot\frac7{25}+\frac5{13}\cdot\frac{24}{25}=\frac{84+120}{325}=\frac{204}{325}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{204}{325}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-06.title: Split into cases
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-06.body:
The box sizes are either $3,1,1$ or $2,2,1$.
- $3,1,1$: choose the box with three letters ($3$ ways), its three letters ($\binom53=10$), then which of the remaining two letters goes to the first of the other boxes ($2$): $3\cdot10\cdot2=60$.
- $2,2,1$: choose the box with one letter ($3$), its letter ($5$), then two of the remaining four letters for the next box ($\binom42=6$): $3\cdot5\cdot6=90$.

Total: $60+90=150$.

**Answer: 150**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-06.title: Inclusion-exclusion
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-06.body:
Each of the $5$ letters can go into any of $3$ boxes: $3^5=243$. Subtract those missing at least one box: $\binom31 2^5-\binom32 1^5=96-3=93$. So $243-93=150$.

**Answer: 150**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-07.title: Law of cosines
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-07.body:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the sides $\sqrt5$ and $\sqrt6$. Then $\cos\theta=\frac{5+6-7}{2\sqrt{30}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{30}}$, so $\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-\frac4{30}}=\sqrt{\frac{13}{15}}$. The area is
$$\tfrac12\sqrt{30}\sqrt{\tfrac{13}{15}}=\tfrac12\sqrt{26}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt{26}}{2}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-10.title: Difference of cubes
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-10.body:
Let $a=\sqrt[3]7$. Since $a^3-1=(a-1)(a^2+a+1)$, multiply numerator and denominator by $a^2+a+1$:
$$\frac{1}{a-1}=\frac{a^2+a+1}{a^3-1}=\frac{\sqrt[3]{49}+\sqrt[3]{7}+1}{6}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt[3]{49}+\sqrt[3]{7}+1}{6}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-11.title: Tests for 9 and 11
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-11.body:
Divisible by $9$: the digit sum $32+a+b$ is a multiple of $9$, so $a+b=4$ or $13$.

Divisible by $11$: the alternating sum $(1-7)\cdot4+a-b=a-b-24$ is a multiple of $11$, so $a-b=2$ or $-9$.

$a+b$ and $a-b$ have the same parity, so $a+b=4$, $a-b=2$ (giving $a=3,b=1$) or $a+b=13$, $a-b=-9$ (giving $a=2,b=11$, not a digit). So $(a,b)=(3,1)$.

**Answer: $(3,1)$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-11.title: Two-digit blocks
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-11.body:
Since $100\equiv1\pmod{99}$, a number is congruent mod $99$ to the sum of its two-digit blocks: $17+17+17+17+\overline{ab}=68+\overline{ab}$. This is divisible by $99$ exactly when $\overline{ab}=31$.

**Answer: $(3,1)$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-12.title: Geometric series
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-12.body:
The first six occurs on throw $n$ with probability $\left(\frac56\right)^{n-1}\frac16$. Summing over $n=2,4,6,\dots$:
$$\frac56\cdot\frac16\left(1+\frac{25}{36}+\left(\frac{25}{36}\right)^2+\cdots\right)=\frac{5}{36}\cdot\frac{36}{11}=\frac5{11}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{5}{11}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-12.title: Condition on the first throw
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-12.body:
Let $p$ be the probability of needing an odd number of throws. If the first throw is a six (probability $\frac16$), the count is odd; otherwise ($\frac56$) the remaining count must be even, with probability $1-p$. So $p=\frac16+\frac56(1-p)$, giving $p=\frac6{11}$; the answer is $1-p=\frac5{11}$.

**Answer: $\frac{5}{11}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-13.title: Evaluate the inner logs
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-13.body:
$\log_{16}4=\frac12$ since $16^{1/2}=4$, and $\log_5125=3$. So the expression is $\log_2\left(\frac12\right)^3=\log_2\frac18=-3$.

**Answer: $-3$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-14.title: Edge cubes
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-14.body:
A unit cube has exactly two painted faces when it is on an edge but not at a corner. Each of the $12$ edges has $n-2$ such cubes, so $12(n-2)=180$, $n-2=15$, $n=17$.

**Answer: 17**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-15.title: Vieta
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-15.body:
There are $500$ factors, so the coefficient of $x^{499}$ is minus the sum of the roots: $-(2+4+\cdots+1000)=-2(1+2+\cdots+500)=-2\cdot\frac{500\cdot501}{2}=-250500$.

**Answer: $-250500$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-16.title: Factor
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-16.body:
Let $t=[2x]$. Then $2t^2-9t+9=(2t-3)(t-3)=0$, so $t=\frac32$ or $t=3$. Since $t$ is an integer, $[2x]=3$, i.e. $3\le 2x<4$, so $\frac32\le x<2$.

**Answer: $\frac32\le x<2$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-17.title: Cyclic quadrilateral
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-17.body:
Since $\angle B=\angle D=90^\circ$, $ABCD$ is inscribed in the circle with diameter $AC$. In triangle $BCD$, by the law of cosines $BD^2=1+4-2\cdot2\cdot1\cos120^\circ=7$. By the law of sines in that circle, $AC=2R=\frac{BD}{\sin120^\circ}=\frac{\sqrt7}{\sqrt3/2}=\frac{2\sqrt7}{\sqrt3}$. Then from right triangle $ABC$,
$$AB^2=AC^2-BC^2=\frac{28}{3}-4=\frac{16}{3},\qquad AB=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}=\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-17.title: Coordinates
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-17.body:
Put $C=(0,0)$, $B=(2,0)$, and $D=(\cos120^\circ,\sin120^\circ)=\left(-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)$. The right angle at $B$ puts $A$ on the line $x=2$: $A=(2,h)$. The right angle at $D$ means $\vec{DA}\cdot\vec{DC}=0$: $\left(\frac52,h-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)\cdot\left(\frac12,-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=\frac54-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}h+\frac34=0$, so $h=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}$. Thus $AB=h=\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}$.

**Answer: $\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-18.title: Cube roots of unity
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-18.body:
$x^2+x+1=0$, so $x$ is a primitive cube root of unity $\omega$, with $\omega^3=1$. Since $2^n$ is never a multiple of $3$, $x^{2^n}$ is $\omega$ or $\omega^2$, and $f(2^n)=\omega+\omega^2=-1$ in either case. Sum: $-1990$.

**Answer: $-1990$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-19.title: Complementary angles
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-19.body:
In a right triangle with hypotenuse $\pi$ and a leg $1$, the angle $x$ opposite the leg has $\sin x=\frac1\pi$ and the other acute angle $y$ has $\cos y=\frac1\pi$. So $x=\operatorname{Arcsin}\frac1\pi$, $y=\operatorname{Arccos}\frac1\pi$, and $x+y=90^\circ$. Hence the value is $\cot90^\circ=0$.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-20.title: Triangle ACE
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-20.body:
By symmetry, the chords $AC$, $CE$, $EA$ each cut off one short and one long arc, so triangle $ACE$ is equilateral and inscribed in the circle. The inscribed angle $\angle ABC$ subtends the arc $AEC$, which is $\frac23$ of the circle, so $\angle ABC=120^\circ$. By the law of cosines,
$$AC^2=2^2+10^2-2\cdot2\cdot10\cos120^\circ=124.$$
The area is $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot124=31\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $31\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-22.title: Stars and bars
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-22.body:
The terms are $x^ay^bz^c$ with $a+b+c=17$, $a,b,c\ge0$. The number of such triples is $\binom{19}{2}=171$.

**Answer: 171**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-22.title: Expand by powers of x
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-22.body:
Write $(x+(y+z))^{17}=\sum_k\binom{17}{k}x^{17-k}(y+z)^k$. The factor $(y+z)^k$ has $k+1$ terms, and different $k$ give different powers of $x$, so the total is $1+2+\cdots+18=171$.

**Answer: 171**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-23.title: Two substitutions
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-23.body:
$x=2$: $2f(2)+\sqrt2f(\frac12)=4$. $x=\frac12$: $\sqrt2 f(2)+2f(\frac12)=\sqrt2$. Multiply the second by $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$: $f(2)+\sqrt2f(\frac12)=1$. Subtracting from the first: $f(2)=3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-24.title: Sum over a
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-24.body:
For a fixed $a$, the first $4a$ flips must be exactly: heads on flips $1,\dots,a-1$, tails on flip $a$, heads on flips $a+1,\dots,4a-1$, tails on flip $4a$. That specific sequence has probability $\left(\frac12\right)^{4a}$. Summing over $a=1,2,3,\dots$:
$$\sum_{a\ge1}\left(\frac1{16}\right)^a=\frac{1/16}{1-1/16}=\frac1{15}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{1}{15}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-25.title: Perfect square
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-25.body:
Rearranging, $16(\log x)^2-24\log x\log y+9(\log y)^2=(4\log x-3\log y)^2=0$. So $3\log y=4\log x$, i.e. $y^3=x^4$ and $y=x^{4/3}=\sqrt[3]{x^4}$.

**Answer: $y=x^{4/3}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-26.title: Complex numbers
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-26.body:
$\operatorname{Arctan}\frac1x$ is the argument of $x+i$. The product $(1+i)(2+i)(3+i)=(1+3i)(3+i)=10i$ has argument $\frac\pi2$, and since each angle is in $(0,\frac\pi4]$ the sum is exactly $\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi}{2}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-27.title: Diagonal of a right angle
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-27.body:
Let $A,B,C$ be consecutive vertices with $AB=1$, $BC=2$. Each interior angle is $135^\circ$, so
$$AC^2=1+4-2\cdot1\cdot2\cos135^\circ=5+2\sqrt2.$$
By symmetry the arcs $AB$ and $BC$ together make a quarter of the circle, so $AC$ subtends a central angle of $90^\circ$ and $AC=R\sqrt2$. Hence $R^2=\frac{5+2\sqrt2}{2}=\sqrt2+\frac52$ and the area is $\pi\left(\sqrt2+\frac52\right)$.

**Answer: $\left(1,\frac52\right)$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-28.title: x + 3/2 is a perfect square
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-28.body:
Let $n=[2x]$, an integer. Then $x=n^2-\frac32$, so $2x=2n^2-3$ is an integer and $[2x]=2n^2-3$. Hence $2n^2-3=n$, i.e. $(2n-3)(n+1)=0$, and as $n$ is an integer, $n=-1$. Then $x=1-\frac32=-\frac12$. Check: $[2x]^2=[-1]^2=1=-\frac12+\frac32$.

**Answer: $x=-\frac12$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-29.title: Choose x so that 4 and 9 appear

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-30.title: Geometric series over rounds
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-30.body:
Al effectively rolls a fair 4-sided die, so he fails to roll a 1 with probability $\frac34$; Joyce fails with $\frac56$; Scott fails with $\frac{11}{12}$. Scott wins in round $k$ if all three fail in the first $k-1$ rounds, then Al and Joyce fail and Scott rolls a 1:
$$P=\sum_{k\ge1}\left(\tfrac34\cdot\tfrac56\cdot\tfrac{11}{12}\right)^{k-1}\tfrac34\cdot\tfrac56\cdot\tfrac1{12}=\frac{5/96}{1-55/96}=\frac{5}{41}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{5}{41}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-30.title: Compare within a round
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniora-30.body:
In any round where the game ends, the winner probabilities are in the ratio $\frac14:\frac34\cdot\frac16:\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac1{12}=\frac14:\frac18:\frac{5}{96}=24:12:5$. So Scott wins with probability $\frac{5}{24+12+5}=\frac5{41}$.

**Answer: $\frac{5}{41}$**
